item.title: Glycine
item.description:
What it is: Glycine is the simplest amino acid, abundant in collagen and gelatin, that supports sleep quality, collagen synthesis, immune function, and cellular repair. Supplementation with glycine has been shown to improve sleep architecture and provide structural and functional benefits across multiple tissues.

Benefits

Sleep Quality & Duration

  • Improves sleep quality and latency (time to fall asleep)
  • May extend slow-wave sleep (deep sleep)
  • Enhances sleep restoration
  • Reduces sleep disturbances
  • Results visible within 1-2 nights

Collagen & Connective Tissue

  • Essential amino acid for collagen synthesis
  • Supports skin elasticity and firmness
  • Supports joint and ligament health
  • Supports bone health
  • One-third of collagen is glycine

Immune Function

  • Supports immune cell function
  • Supports glutathione synthesis (master antioxidant)
  • Enhances immune resilience
  • Complements immune strategies

Muscle & Athletic Performance

  • Component of muscle tissue
  • Supports creatine synthesis
  • May improve strength and power
  • Supports recovery post-exercise

Joint & Bone Health

  • Essential for cartilage synthesis
  • Supports synovial fluid
  • Supports bone collagen matrix
  • Joint resilience support

Dosage

Sleep support: 3,000-5,000 mg evening before bed Collagen + general: 2,000-3,000 mg daily Full spectrum: 3,000-5,000 mg daily Timing: Evening before bed for sleep; with meals for general support Duration: Results visible within 1-2 nights for sleep; weeks for collagen benefits

item.title: Taurine
item.description:
What it is: Taurine is a semi-essential amino acid synthesized from methionine and cysteine, abundant in the heart, brain, and muscles. It supports cardiac function, exercise performance, neurological health, and cellular energy production—making it valuable for cardiovascular optimization and athletic performance.

Benefits

Cardiac Function & Heart Health

  • Strengthens cardiac contractility (force of heart contraction)
  • Supports healthy heart rhythm
  • Supports cardiovascular resilience
  • May improve exercise tolerance
  • Reduces cardiovascular disease markers

Athletic Performance & Recovery

  • Improves endurance and power output
  • Reduces exercise-induced fatigue
  • Accelerates recovery post-exercise
  • Supports muscle performance
  • Particularly effective for high-intensity exercise

Neurological Support

  • Supports brain cell function
  • Protective against neurological stress
  • Supports neurological aging
  • Neuroprotective mechanisms
  • Cognitive function support

Eye Health

  • Concentrated in retina
  • Supports visual function
  • Protective against vision aging
  • Essential for retinal health

Metabolic & Energy Support

  • Supports mitochondrial function
  • Enhances ATP production
  • Supports cellular energy metabolism
  • Metabolic optimization

Dosage

Cardiac support: 1,000-1,500 mg daily Athletic focus: 1,500-2,000 mg daily Full spectrum: 2,000-3,000 mg daily Timing: With meals (especially post-workout) Duration: 2-4 weeks for initial effects; 8+ weeks for full benefits

item.title: 5-HTP (5-Hydroxytryptophan)
item.description:
What Is 5-HTP?

5-HTP (5-Hydroxytryptophan) is a naturally occurring amino acid and direct precursor to serotonin, the neurotransmitter responsible for mood, sleep, appetite, pain perception, and impulse control. It’s synthesized from the essential amino acid tryptophan, using vitamin B6 and magnesium as cofactors.

Key biochemistry:

  • Tryptophan (dietary) → 5-HTP (via TPH enzyme) → Serotonin
  • 5-HTP supplements bypass the first conversion step, directly increasing serotonin synthesis
  • Primary source for clinical use: Griffonia simplicifolia seed extract (naturally contains 20-30% 5-HTP)

item.title: GABA (Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid)
item.description:
What Is GABA?

GABA (gamma-aminobutyric acid) is the brain’s primary inhibitory neurotransmitter, found in approximately 30-40% of brain synapses. Unlike excitatory neurotransmitters like glutamate that activate neurons, GABA dampens neuronal firing, reducing the overall excitability of the nervous system.

Your body synthesizes GABA from the amino acid glutamate via the enzyme glutamate decarboxylase (GAD), which requires vitamin B6 as a cofactor. During stress, anxiety, poor sleep, or chronic stimulation (caffeine, nootropics), GABA synthesis may become insufficient, leading to nervous system hyperexcitability.

item.title: L-Tryptophan
item.description:
What Is L-Tryptophan?

L-Tryptophan is an essential amino acid, meaning your body cannot synthesize it and must obtain it from diet or supplementation. It’s a large neutral amino acid with a critical role as the precursor to serotonin, melatonin, niacin (vitamin B3), and quinolinic acid.

Key biochemistry:

  • Tryptophan (dietary/supplemental) → 5-HTP (via TPH enzyme) → Serotonin
  • Tryptophan → Melatonin (via serotonin pathway in pineal gland)
  • Tryptophan → Niacin via kynurenine pathway (produces 1mg niacin per 60mg tryptophan)
  • Tryptophan → Quinolinic acid (neuromodulator; affects mood and cognition)

item.title: L-Tyrosine
item.description:
What Is L-Tyrosine?

L-Tyrosine is a conditionally essential amino acid that serves as the primary precursor to dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine (the catecholamine neurotransmitters responsible for motivation, focus, and stress response). While your body can synthesize tyrosine from phenylalanine, endogenous production becomes insufficient under stress, intense mental effort, or physical strain.

Key biochemistry:

  • L-Phenylalanine → L-Tyrosine (via phenylalanine hydroxylase)
  • L-Tyrosine → L-DOPA (via tyrosine hydroxylase; requires iron and vitamin B6)
  • L-DOPA → Dopamine (via DOPA decarboxylase; requires vitamin B6)
  • Dopamine → Norepinephrine (via dopamine-β-hydroxylase; requires copper and vitamin C)
  • Norepinephrine → Epinephrine (via phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase)

This cascade is the catecholamine pathway — the “go” neurotransmitter system. Unlike serotonin (mood and calm), dopamine drives motivation, focus, drive, and assertiveness.
